problemStatement.formal: theorem elementary_quadratic_reciprocity {p q : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hq2 : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q) : legendreSym q p * legendreSym p q = (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2))
problemStatement.plain: For distinct odd primes p and q, the product of Legendre symbols (q/p)(p/q) = (-1)^((p-1)/2 * (q-1)/2). Proven via Eisenstein's elementary approach using Gauss's Lemma, floor function sums, and lattice point counting.
whyMatters: Quadratic reciprocity is one of the most celebrated theorems in number theory
The elementary Eisenstein proof uses only basic arithmetic and counting
Over 240 known proofs exist; this formalizes one of the most elegant

proven: Full QR via elementary proof chain
Eisenstein proof chain theorem (all 3 steps in one statement)
First supplementary law (-1 is QR iff p ≡ 1 mod 4)
Second supplementary law (2 is QR iff p ≡ ±1 mod 8)
open: Gauss sum proof (no Gauss sum module in Mathlib)
